name: Jehoram
bio:
Jehoram succeeded his father Jehoshaphat as king of Judah after Jehoshaphat's twenty-five-year reign ended and he was buried with his ancestors in the City of David (1 Kings 22:50).

## 📖 Core Story: Marriage into Ahab's House

Jehoram began to reign over Judah at thirty-two, in the fifth year of Joram (Jehoram) son of Ahab, and reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, as Ahab's house had, because he had married Ahab's daughter Athaliah, and he did evil in the LORD's eyes — though the LORD spared Judah from destruction for David's sake. In his reign, Edom revolted from Judah's rule and set up its own king; Jehoram struck the surrounding Edomites by night at Zair, but Edom's revolt succeeded anyway, and Libnah revolted at the same time (2 Kings 8:16-24).

Chronicles tells more of this reign. As soon as he was established on the throne, Jehoram killed all his brothers, to whom Jehoshaphat had given rich gifts and fortified cities, along with some of Israel's officials. A letter came to him from the prophet Elijah, pronouncing that because he had led Judah into the whoredoms of Ahab's house and murdered brothers better than himself, the LORD would strike his people, his children, his wives, and all he owned with a great plague, and strike him with an incurable disease of the bowels. The LORD then stirred up the Philistines and Arabs, who invaded Judah, plundered the palace, and carried off all his sons and wives except the youngest, Jehoahaz (that is, Ahaziah). Jehoram then suffered the disease exactly as foretold, dying in agony after two years when his bowels failed; the people lit no funeral fire for him as they had for his ancestors, and he was buried in the City of David but not among the kings, "to no one's regret" (2 Chronicles 21:1-20).
